% figure registry (figdefs.tex is generated by the extract step)
\newcommand{\qfigdef}[4]{\@namedef{qf@file@#1}{#2}\@namedef{qf@w@#1}{#3}\@namedef{qf@wide@#1}{#4}}
\newcommand{\qf@check}[1]{\@ifundefined{qf@file@#1}{\PackageError{score2}{Unknown figure id #1}{}}{}}
\newcommand{\qf@img}[4][]{\includegraphics[width=#2\dimexpr\@nameuse{qf@w@#4}pt\relax,max width=#3,max height=0.45\textheight,#1]{\@nameuse{qf@file@#4}}}
% Full-width questions: finalize wraps every question that contains a wide figure in \qfullbegin...\qfullend,
% so the WHOLE question (stem, figures, options) is set across the page in reading order, then the two columns
% resume. The question's head - its number, stem and first figure (\qfullsplit marks the end of the head) -
% is kept on one page, so a number is never left at a page foot with its figure overleaf; the rest may break
% across pages normally, so no big gaps are left. Without a \qfullsplit, the whole question is kept together
% if it is under 45% of a page. Never write these yourself.
\newif\ifqf@full
\newif\ifqf@boxed
\newsavebox{\qf@box}
\newcommand{\qf@open}{\global\qf@fulltrue\par\global\qf@boxedtrue
  \setbox\qf@box\vbox\bgroup\hsize\textwidth\linewidth\textwidth}
\newcommand{\qf@emit}[1]{\par\egroup\global\qf@boxedfalse
  \ifdim\dimexpr\ht\qf@box+\dp\qf@box\relax<#1\textheight\noindent\usebox{\qf@box}\par\else\unvbox\qf@box\fi}
\newcommand{\qfullsplit}{\ifqf@boxed\qf@emit{0.85}\fi}
\newcommand{\qf@close}{\ifqf@boxed\qf@emit{0.45}\fi\global\qf@fullfalse}
\newcommand{\qfullbegin}{\end{multicols}\qf@open}
\newcommand{\qfullend}{\qf@close\begin{multicols}{2}}
\newcommand{\qfullstart}{\qf@open}
\newcommand{\qfulldone}{\qf@close}
% \qfig[scale]{id}: block figure, centred, directly where it is written (size set by the tool).
% Fallback if a wide figure is not inside a full-width question: break out of the columns in place - no floats.
\newcommand{\qfig}[2][1]{\qf@check{#2}%
  \ifqf@full\qf@blk{#1}{#2}\else
  \ifnum\@nameuse{qf@wide@#2}=1 \expandafter\@firstoftwo\else\expandafter\@secondoftwo\fi
  {\end{multicols}\begin{center}\qf@img{#1}{\textwidth}{#2}\end{center}\begin{multicols}{2}}%
  {\qf@blk{#1}{#2}}\fi}
\newcommand{\qf@blk}[2]{\par\smallskip{\centering\qf@img{#1}{\linewidth}{#2}\par}\smallskip}
% \qfigi[scale]{id}: inline figure (inside option lists / tables / minipages); never breaks columns.
\newcommand{\qfigi}[2][1]{\qf@check{#2}\qf@img[valign=c]{#1}{\linewidth}{#2}}
\makeatother
% structure macros - lint reads these to check completeness and figure placement
\newcommand{\papersec}[1]{\par\bigskip{\centering\Large\bfseries PAPER-#1\par}\medskip}
\newcommand{\partsec}[2]{\par\medskip\noindent{\large\bfseries PART-#1: #2}\par\smallskip}
\newcommand{\sect}[1]{\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{#1}\par}
\newcommand{\qn}[1]{\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{#1.}~}
\newcommand{\paraq}[2]{\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Paragraph for Questions #1 and #2}\par}
\newenvironment{qoptions}{\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.8em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=2pt,label={}]}{\end{itemize}}
\newcommand{\opt}[2]{\item[(#1)] #2}

\partsec{1}{PHYSICS}
\sect{SECTION-I(i)}
\qn{1} A variable capacitor with initial capacitance C$_0$ is charged to a voltage V$_0$ and is short circuited through a resistance R. If current remains constant during discharging (an external agent is pulling the plates apart) then choose correct option(s).
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{Variation of capacitance with time is given by C = C$_0\left(1-\dfrac{t}{RC_0}\right)$.}
\opt{B}{Time taken to discharge the capacitor is given by t = RC$_0$.}
\opt{C}{Total heat produced in the resistor is C$_0$V$_0^2$.}
\opt{D}{Initial energy stored in the capacitor is $\dfrac12$C$_0$V$_0^2$.}
\end{qoptions}
\qn{2} A cylindrical body of radius R is fixed in a horizontal position. A piece of ideal thread of length $\ell$ was laid on its slippery surface. On one end of thread a point like body of mass m is attached, while to the other end another point like body of mass 2m is attached . Choose correct statement(s). The system is in equilibrium.\par
\qfig{p1_phy_s1_q02_1}
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{2 sin$\alpha$ = sin$\beta$}
\opt{B}{2 sin$\beta$ = sin$\alpha$}
\opt{C}{Maximum possible length of string is $\ell_{\max}$ = 2$\pi$R/3.}
\opt{D}{Maximum possible length of string is $\ell_{\max}$ = 2R.}
\end{qoptions}
\qn{3} By properly combining two prisms made of different materials, it is possible to :-
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{have dispersion without average deviation.}
\opt{B}{have deviation without dispersion.}
\opt{C}{have both dispersion and average deviation.}
\opt{D}{have neither dispersion nor average deviation.}
\end{qoptions}
\qn{4} A sample of ideal gas of some mass is taken through the cyclic process shown in the figure. The temperature of the gas at state A is T$_\mathrm A$ = 200 K, and at state C is T$_\mathrm C$ = 1800 K. Choose the correct option(s) :-\par
\qfig{p1_phy_s1_q04_1}
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$\dfrac{V_A}{V_C}=\dfrac13$}
\opt{B}{$\dfrac{V_A}{V_B}=\dfrac19$}
\opt{C}{$\dfrac{P_AV_A}{P_CV_C}=\dfrac13$}
\opt{D}{$\dfrac{P_AV_A}{P_CV_C}=\dfrac19$}
\end{qoptions}
\qn{5} X-ray from a tube with a target A of atomic number Z shows strong K lines for target A and weak K lines for impurities. The wavelength of K$_\alpha$ lines is $\lambda_z$ for target A and $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$ for two impurities. If $\dfrac{\lambda_z}{\lambda_1}$ = 4 and $\dfrac{\lambda_z}{\lambda_2}=\dfrac14$. Screening constant of K$_\alpha$ lines to be unity. Select the correct statement(s).
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{The atomic number of first impurity is 2Z $-$ 1.}
\opt{B}{The atomic number of first impurity is 2Z + 1.}
\opt{C}{The atomic number of second impurity is $\dfrac{(Z+1)}2$.}
\opt{D}{The atomic number of second impurity is $\dfrac Z2$ + 1.}
\end{qoptions}
\qn{6} A man is sitting in a boat floating in water. There are heavy stones placed in the boat.
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{When the man throws the stones in water, the level of boat goes down.}
\opt{B}{When the man throws the stones in water, the level of boat rises up.}
\opt{C}{When the man drinks some water, the level of boat goes down}
\opt{D}{When the man drinks some water, the level of boat remains unchanged.}
\end{qoptions}
\sect{SECTION-I(ii)}
\qn{7} A block of mass 1.0 kg is pulled up on a rough slope of inclination 37$^\circ$ with the horizontal. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the slope is 0.25. The block moves with acceleration 2.0 m/s$^2$. After 5.0 s from the instant the block starts, which of the following statements is/are true ? (Power of any force is given by P = $\vec F\cdot\vec V$)\par
{\footnotesize\setlength{\tabcolsep}{1.5pt}\noindent\begin{tabular}{|c|L{3.6cm}|c|L{2.0cm}|}
\hline
 & \multicolumn{1}{>{\centering\arraybackslash}p{3.6cm}|}{List-I} & & \multicolumn{1}{>{\centering\arraybackslash}p{2.0cm}|}{List-II} \\ \hline
(I) & Power delivered by the pulling force & (P) & 20 W \\ \hline
(II) & Power delivered by the weight of the block & (Q) & $-$20 W \\ \hline
(III) & Power delivered by the friction between the slope and the block & (R) & $-$60 W \\ \hline
(IV) & Power delivered by the contact force between the slope and the block & (S) & 100 W \\ \hline
 & & (T) & 80 W \\ \hline
\end{tabular}}\par
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{I $\to$ P;II $\to$ R;III $\to$ Q;IV $\to$ S}
\opt{B}{I $\to$ S;II $\to$ R;III $\to$ Q;IV $\to$ Q}
\opt{C}{I $\to$ P;II $\to$ Q;III $\to$ R;IV $\to$ S}
\opt{D}{I $\to$ Q;II $\to$ S;III $\to$ T;IV $\to$ P}
\end{qoptions}
\qn{8} A disc of mass m and radius R is performing pure rolling on the inclined surface of a wedge of mass M. Wedge is placed on a rough horizontal surface. If wedge does not move on the horizontal surface then match the followings.\par
\qfig{p1_phy_s2_q08_1}
{\footnotesize\setlength{\tabcolsep}{1.5pt}\noindent\begin{tabular}{|c|L{2.0cm}|c|L{4.0cm}|}
\hline
 & \multicolumn{1}{>{\centering\arraybackslash}p{2.0cm}|}{List-I} & & \multicolumn{1}{>{\centering\arraybackslash}p{4.0cm}|}{List-II} \\ \hline
(I) & Frictional force acting on disc & (P) & $\dfrac{mg\sin\theta}{3}$ \\ \hline
(II) & Vertical component of net frictional force acting on wedge & (Q) & $\dfrac{mg\sin^2\theta}{3}$ \\ \hline
(III) & Normal reaction acting on disc & (R) & mg$\cos\theta$ \\ \hline
(IV) & Normal reaction acting on wedge by the ground & (S) & $\left(m\cos^2\theta+\dfrac m3\sin^2\theta+M\right)g$ \\ \hline
 & & (T) & $\left(m\sin^2\theta+\dfrac m3\cos^2\theta+M\right)g$ \\ \hline
\end{tabular}}\par
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{I $\to$ P;II $\to$ Q;III $\to$ S;IV $\to$ T}
\opt{B}{I $\to$ P;II $\to$ Q;III $\to$ T;IV $\to$ S}
\opt{C}{I $\to$ P;II $\to$ Q;III $\to$ R;IV $\to$ S}
\opt{D}{I $\to$ S;II $\to$ T;III $\to$ P;IV $\to$ Q}
\end{qoptions}
\qn{9} Match the following lists.\par
{\footnotesize\setlength{\tabcolsep}{1.5pt}\noindent\begin{tabular}{|c|L{3.0cm}|c|L{3.0cm}|}
\hline
 & \multicolumn{1}{>{\centering\arraybackslash}p{3.0cm}|}{List$-$I} & & \multicolumn{1}{>{\centering\arraybackslash}p{3.0cm}|}{List$-$II} \\ \hline
(I) & Nearby objects appear moving past faster than distant objects. & (P) & Human eye sense the direction from which light enters it. \\ \hline

\begin{qoptions}

\opt{C}{I $\to$ P;II $\to$ S;III $\to$ R;IV $\to$ P}

\end{qoptions}

List I corresponds to height of liquid in right limb and list II corresponds to radius of meniscus (R) and its shape in left limb.\par

\sect{SECTION-II}
\qn{1} In a long cylindrical metal wire of radius r and of resistivity $\rho$, a current of strength I flows in uniform distribution. The wire has constant surface temperature T$_0$. The temperature of the wire on its axis of symmetry is given by T = T$_\mathrm o$ + $\dfrac{I^2\rho}{\pi^2r^2K}\times\lambda$. Here K is thermal conductivity of wire. Find $\lambda$.
\qn{2} A certain amount of water is heated from 20$^\circ$C to 40$^\circ$C using an 800 Watt immersion heater. We expect to heat water in 210 seconds, but instead it takes 230 seconds. Determine the heat capacity of vessel in S.I. units. Ignore other heat losses.
\qn{3} A mass M is divided in two parts m and M$-$m. Now two parts are connected by an ideal string passing over a pulley as shown in diagram. Find value of m/M such that tension in string is maximum.\par
\qfig{p1_phy_s3_q03_1}
\qn{4} A cell of emf 1.5 V and internal resistance 0.5 $\Omega$ is connected to a nonlinear conductor in which current varies with voltage as V$^2$ = I. Calculate the current drawn from cell (in ampere).
\qn{5} A coil with inductance L and resistance R is connected to an alternating source. The capacity of a capacitor that can be connected in series later with the coil such that active power of circuit does not change is given by\par C = $\dfrac{n}{\omega^2L}$. Find value of n.
\qn{6} Consider a spherical homogeneous cloud of mass M made by an explosion. Due to energy received from the explosion, it is expanding and the expansion is spherically symmetric. At an instant its radius is R$_0$ and the particles on the surface are moving away from its center with velocity V$_0$. Its radius when expansion ceases is given by\par $\dfrac{nGMR_0}{2GM-R_0V_0^2}$. Find n.
\qn{7} The electrostatic flux through a rectangular area of $\dfrac7{188}$m$^2$ is lying in a plane 2x + 3y + 6z = 10 due to an electric field (8$\hat i$ + 6$\hat j$ + 10$\hat k$) V/m will be in (V-m)
\qn{8} A parallel beam of light of all wavelength greater than 3000 \AA\ falls on a double slit in a Young's double slit experiment. It is observed that the wavelengths 3600\AA\ and 6000\AA\ are absent at a distance of 31.5 mm from the position of the central maximum, and the orders of the minima at this point for the two wavelengths differ by 7. If the distance between the slits and the screen is 1m, the separation between the two slits (in mm) is :

\opt{B}{\qfigi{p1_chem_s1_q01_B}}

\opt{B}{\qfigi{p1_chem_s1_q02_B}}

\qn{3} In which of the following process(es) electrons are removed from different type of orbitals?

\qn{1} A current carrying wire is placed along ACB in the grooves of an insulating semicircular disc of radius `R' as shown. The current enters at point A and leaves at point B. Determine the magnetic field at point D.\par
\qfig{p2_phy_s1_q01_1}
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$\dfrac{\mu_0i}{8\pi R\sqrt3}$}
\opt{B}{$\dfrac{\mu_0i}{4\pi R\sqrt3}$}
\opt{C}{$\dfrac{\sqrt3\mu_0i}{4\pi R}$}
\opt{D}{None}
\end{qoptions}
\qn{2} In the following radioactive decay C is stable nucleus. Then\par
$\mathrm A\xrightarrow{\lambda_1}\mathrm B\xrightarrow{\lambda_2}\mathrm C$\par
time t = 0 \quad N$_0$ \quad 0 \quad 0\par
time t \quad N$_1$ \quad N$_2$ \quad N$_3$
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{Number of nuclei of B will first increase and then decrease.}
\opt{B}{Rate of decay of A will first increase and then decrease.}
\opt{C}{If $\lambda_2>\lambda_1$ then activity of B will always be higher than activity of A.}
\opt{D}{If $\lambda_1>\lambda_2$ then number of nuclei of C will always be less than number of nuclei of B.}
\end{qoptions}

\qfig{p2_phy_s1_q03_1}

\qn{5} The main scale of a vernier calipers reads in mm and its vernier is divided into 10 divisions which coincides with 9 divisions of the main scale. It was also observed when two jaws are brought in contact the zero of the vernier scale coincided with the zero of the main scale. The length of a cube is measured with this vernier calipers. The main scale reads 10 mm and the first division of the vernier scale coincides with the main scale. If the mass of the cube is 2.0606 g then mark the correct alternatives.
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{The density of the cube in appropriate significant figures is 2.0000 gm/cm$^3$.}
\opt{B}{The density of the cube in appropriate significant figures is 2.00 g/cm$^3$.}
\opt{C}{If the zero mark of the vernier scale lies towards the left side of the zero of the main scale when the two jaws are brought in contact, the error will be positive and the correction will be negative.}
\opt{D}{If the zero mark of the vernier scale lies towards the right side of the zero of the main scale when two jaws are brought in contact the error will be positive and the correction will be negative.}
\end{qoptions}
\qn{6} For the given potential versus distance graph for one dimensional electric field and a particle of charge 20 $\mu$C and mass 0.2 kg, Choose the correct option(s).\par
\qfig{p2_phy_s2_q06_1}
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{Force acting on the particle at x = 25 cm is zero.}
\opt{B}{Force acting on the particle at x = 25 cm is 4$\hat{\mathrm i}$ Newton.}
\opt{C}{Minimum speed at origin required by the particle to reach x = 25 cm is 2 m/s.}
\opt{D}{Minimum speed at origin required by the particle to reach x = 25 cm is $\sqrt2$ m/s.}
\end{qoptions}
\qn{7} A sky lab of mass m is first launched from the surface of earth (radius R) in a circular orbit of radius 2R (from centre of earth) and then it is shifted from this circular orbit to another circular orbit of radius 3R.
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{Minimum energy required to place the lab in first orbit is equal to $\dfrac34$ mgR.}
\opt{B}{Minimum energy required to shift the lab from first orbit to second orbit is $\dfrac{mgR}{12}$.}
\opt{C}{Energy of sky lab in second orbit is greater than its energy in first orbit.}
\opt{D}{Energy of sky lab in second orbit is less than its energy in first orbit.}
\end{qoptions}

\qfig{p2_phy_s2_q08_1}

\opt{C}{$\Delta\mathrm U_{\mathrm{CA}}$ = $-$ve}

\qn{9} A ball of mass m moving horizontally at a speed v collides with the bob of a simple pendulum at rest. The mass of the bob is also m. Here v $\leqslant$ $\sqrt{2g\ell}$. (Where $\ell$ is length of the pendulum)
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{If the collision is perfectly inelastic, the height to which the two balls rise after the collision is $\dfrac{v^2}{8g}$.}
\opt{B}{If the collision is perfectly inelastic, the kinetic energy of the system immediately after the collision becomes half of that before collision.}
\opt{C}{If the collision is perfectly elastic, the bob of the pendulum will rise to a height of $\dfrac{v^2}{2g}$.}
\opt{D}{If the collision is perfectly elastic, the kinetic energy of the system immediately after the collision is equal to that before collision.}
\end{qoptions}
\qn{10} A pulley of radius R = 20 cm is rotated by a weight suspended from a thread which is gradually being wound off the pulley. Initially the weight is at rest and then it begins to go down with an acceleration a = 2 cm/s$^2$ :-\par
\qfig{p2_phy_s2_q10_1}
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{Angular velocity of the pulley when the weight has travelled a distance S$_1$ = 100 cm is 1rad/s.}
\opt{B}{Angular velocity of the pulley when the weight has travelled a distance S$_1$ = 100 cm is 2rad/s.}
\opt{C}{The magnitude of the acceleration of point A when the weight has travelled a distance S$_1$ = 100 cm is $20\sqrt2$ cm/s$^2$.}
\opt{D}{The magnitude of the acceleration of point A when the weight has travelled a distance S$_1$ = 100 cm is 20.1 cm/s$^2$.}
\end{qoptions}
\sect{SECTION-III}
\qn{1} Two thin lenses with lens powers D$_1$ and D$_2$ diopter are located at distance L = 25 cm from each other and their optical axes coincide. This system creates an erect real image of the object, located at the optical axis closer to lens D$_1$ with the net magnification M$_1$ = 1. If the position of the two lenses are exchanged, the system again produces an erect real image with the net magnification M$_2$ = 4. What is the difference between lens powers $\Delta$D = D$_1$ $-$ D$_2$ (in diopter)?
\qn{2} A storage battery (E = 24 V) was connected to one end of a two conductor telephone line of length L=5.6 km. There is a leakage somewhere in the line. If the free ends are open, then current through the battery is I$_1$ = 1.6 A and if the free ends of the line are short-circuited then current through the battery is I$_2$ = 2 A. The short-circuit current of the battery is I$_3$ = 24 A and resistance of each conductor is r = 7$\Omega$. Determine the resistance (in $\Omega$) of the insulation R at the point of the breakdown.
\qn{3} A string will break apart if it is placed under too much tensile stress. One type of steel has density $\rho_{\mathrm{steel}}$ = 10$^4$ kg/m$^3$ and breaking stress $\sigma$ = 9 $\times$ 10$^8$ N/m$^2$. We make a guitar string from (4$\pi$) gram of this type of steel. It should be able to withstand (900$\pi$) N without breaking. The highest possible fundamental frequency (in Hz) of standing waves on the string is 75n. Find n.
\qn{4} A car begins to move at time t = 0 and then accelerates along a straight track with a velocity given by V(t) = 2t$^2$ ms$^{-1}$ for 0 $\leq$ t $\leq$ 2, where t is time in second. After the end of acceleration, the car continues to move at a constant speed. A small block initially at rest on the floor of the car begins to slip at t = 1 s and stops slipping at t = 3 s. The coefficient of static and kinetic friction between the block and the floor are $\mu_\mathrm s$ and $\mu_\mathrm k$ respectively. Find the value of $\dfrac{3\mu_\mathrm s}{\mu_\mathrm k}$.
\qn{5} A plane spiral with a great number N of turns wound tightly to one another is located in a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the spiral's plane. The outside radius of the spiral's turns is equal to a and inner radius is zero. The magnetic induction varies with time as B = B$_0$ sin$\omega$t, where B$_0$ and $\omega$ are constants. Find the amplitude of emf induced in the spiral. (Given : $\omega=\dfrac1\pi$ rad/s, N = 1000, a = 3cm, B$_0$ = 10 Tesla)
\qn{6} A steel rod is 4.000 cm in diameter at 30$^\circ$C. A brass ring has an interior diameter of 3.992 cm at 30$^\circ$C. In order that the ring just slides onto the steel rod, the common temperature of the two should be $\theta$ (in $^\circ$C). Find $\theta$/100 rounded off to nearest integer ($\alpha_{\mathrm{steel}}$ = 11 $\times$ 10$^{-6}$/$^\circ$C and $\alpha_{\mathrm{brass}}$ = 19 $\times$ 10$^{-6}$/$^\circ$C)
\qn{7} A particle of mass 1 mg and charge 1$\mu$C is projected with speed 50 m/s towards a region containing a uniform magnetic field 10 T. What should be the minimum thickness (d) of this region (in m) so that the particle returns back to left side?\par
\qfig{p2_phy_s3_q06_1}
